bug_semantics: containerd CRI StartContainer, for Kubernetes pods with user namespaces (hostUsers:false / NamespaceMode_POD), called updateContainerIOOwner and appended containerd.WithUIDOwner/WithGIDOwner as NewTask options so shim stdio pipes matched the mapped host UID/GID. Pre-fix NewTask option helpers allocated a fresh empty runc options.Options whenever TaskInfo.Options was nil, then NewTask marshaled that object as the shim Create options, replacing the container's runtime options. With SystemdCgroup=true (typical kubelet/containerd), that dropped the systemd cgroup driver flag, so runc treated the systemd-style CgroupsPath as a cgroupfs name and placed the container under system.slice (or another default slice) instead of kubepods.slice. Sandbox/pause stayed in the pod hierarchy; workload containers escaped Kubernetes cpu/memory limits and could DoS the node. v2.0.0 did not take this CRI path; the issue reproduces from 2.0.1 through 2.0.4 with the systemd driver.
flaw_origin: PR #10906 (Fixes #10598, v2.0.0-rc.3 userns /dev/stderr pipe ownership) first wrote updateContainerIOOwner and wired it into StartContainer. That is the smallest public first-write of the userns-only task-option injection. The client already replaced runtime options with any non-nil task Options, but CRI did not pass WithUIDOwner/WithGIDOwner until this commit, so v2.0.0 honored kubepods.slice. A later CRI tweak (018d83650 / #11139) skipped NODE-mode userns for gVisor and left POD-mode vulnerable. The security fix did not revert the IO-owner call; it made NewTask copy runtime options (including SystemdCgroup) before applying task fields (PR #11569 on main, cherry-pick #11618 into v2.0.5).

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: GHSA-cxfp-7pvr-95ff and NVD Analyzed CVE-2025-47291 describe a real CRI cgroup-hierarchy bug for usernamespaced Kubernetes pods (DoS via unenforced limits), not a withdrawn advisory. Public issue #11589 plus rata's bisect identify the CRI IO-owner path added to StartContainer as the regression from v2.0.0 (good) to v2.0.1–2.0.4 (bad) under SystemdCgroup. The mechanism is not a wrong CgroupsPath string in helpers.go; it is that userns-only WithUIDOwner/WithGIDOwner task options replaced runc runtime options and dropped SystemdCgroup, so workload cgroups escaped kubepods.slice.
